description:
📝 Notes
Mar 13, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Mycelium prototype features including the cycle lens, and the visualization of learning processes were discussed.Mycelium Prototype and Cycle LensA prototype was shared for the mycelium focusing on a native Mac morning digest popup that helps the user set intentions for the day based on existing data. The specific "cycle lens" feature was praised for being a niche yet highly valuable demonstration of pattern recognition and value proposition.Visualizer Development and BugsAn update on the “brain” visualizer noted it is working, though currently experiencing a bug where the canvas turns blue upon starting data ingestion. The visualizer is intended to demonstrate how a prompt grows into "learners" or "synapses" that understand data.Testing and System AbstractionThe team agreed to test the visualizer with specific datasets, including personal period-related data, machine activity data, and past R&D conversation transcripts. Discussion explored building self-extending systems that support various mental models by reducing software purpose to answering a question or handling a task.
Details
Project Updates and Document Review: Amir Houieh shared that they had been reading several documents and found that only the last one was relevant from a technical standpoint, noting there were about seven open questions to address (00:00:00). Gabor Kerekes acknowledged that they also had an overview but were curious about the most pressing questions, while Noémi Biró mentioned that they had already dedicated a session to discussing the documents (00:08:11).
Announcement Scheduling: The group discussed scheduling an announcement, with Amir Houieh expressing approval of the message Gabor Kerekes put together. They decided that the best days for an announcement are Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, and agreed to schedule it for Tuesday to maximize reach, as the end of the weekend is not an ideal time for a new AI launch (00:09:33).
Visualizer Development and Update: Amir Houieh provided an update on building a visualizer, referred to as the "drain" or "brain," which is intended to show the feeling of how the system works. They stated that the visualizer is working but currently has some bugs, requiring further development (00:10:39).
Mycelium Prototype: Morning Digest Popup: Noémi Biró shared a prototype for the mycelium focusing on a morning digest popup in a native Mac application. This popup is designed to appear when the user starts their day, taking over the screen to help them set an intention for the day, which the mycelium pulls from existing data sources like emails and calendars (00:10:39).
Focus Visualization and Intentions: The prototype included a calendar view with a visualization of daily focus capacity and was designed to help the user set realistic expectations for the day. The focus capacity is assumed to be learned either by asking the user for confirmation or by accessing time-tracking data like T-metric to identify periods of intense focus (00:13:38).
Cycle Lens Feature: A specific "cycle lens" was prototyped to show how focus capacity relates to the menstrual cycle, suggesting lower energy days (like the first day of the period) and higher energy days (around day 11). The goal of this feature is to encourage the user to set gentle goals on low-energy days or make use of available energy on high-productivity days, serving as a reminder to set realistic commitments (00:16:03).
Value of Niche and Specific Features: Amir Houieh praised the cycle lens idea for being niche, specific, and yet highly valuable, noting that it clearly demonstrates the foundational concepts of pattern recognition and practical value proposition. Gabor Kerekes agreed, suggesting that approaching development from these concrete, specific angles helps build a universal, abstract system that supports all use cases (00:18:17).
Mental Models and Self-Extending Systems: Gabor Kerekes discussed the idea of having different projections or "lenses" for the data and exploring how to support various mental models, such as viewing energy and attention as finite resources (00:21:57). They suggested building a self-extending system where the agent learns how to build tools and skills, possibly drawing inspiration from Open Claw and its use of the PI harness (00:23:01).
Purpose of Software and Generative UI: Amir Houieh offered a high-level abstraction of software's purpose, stating that it should either answer a question or handle a task. They suggested that generative UI becomes powerful if it can be reduced to these two core functions, allowing the system to use tools (UI, diagrams, memory) to respond to a question (00:25:39).
Brain Visualizer Demonstration: Amir Houieh demonstrated the "brain" visualizer, which operates by planting a seed from a prompt (e.g., a product feedback tracker) that grows into "learners" or "synapses" (00:27:00). They noted a bug where the canvas turns blue upon starting data ingestion, which prevents the live visualization of the learners growing, splitting, or merging based on their understanding of the ingested data (00:28:33).
Testing the Visualizer with Real Data: Noémi Biró suggested testing the visualizer with their period-related data to see how the learners operate beneath the surface of the user-facing application (00:30:28). Amir Houieh indicated a willingness to do this and asked Noémi Biró what kind of data they would need, specifying that CSV, JSON, or text files would work, especially if connected to energy levels or feelings (00:32:47).
Testing with Activity Data and R\&D Conversations: Gabor Kerekes suggested trying to use data from an open-source application like Screenpie that tracks activity on the machine as test data. Amir Houieh proposed using data from the group's past R\&D and daily conversation transcripts to train learners focused on individual personalities, projects, and ideas that might otherwise be forgotten (00:33:53).
Safety and Written Output Update: Gabor Kerekes updated the team on their safety work, noting that they finished a sandbox project and had been writing extensively the day before, which they believe is enough material for a blog post (00:35:21).
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will schedule the announcement for next week early, specifically on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday.
Noémi Biró will extract necessary data, including feelings or energy levels, and provide it to Amir Houieh for testing the brain visualization.
Amir Houieh will look into using data from the open-source app, Screen Pi, that tracks activity on the machine for testing.
Amir Houieh will set up learners to analyze all R&D and daily talk conversations to learn about each person's projects, personality, and working style.
